intent: To illustrate the rapid progress and development of Ethiopia, highlighting improvements in health and infrastructure over time.

units.meaning: The health metric shown is child mortality in Ethiopia, measured in percent, tracked from 1990 to 2019.
accepted_routes: Child mortality in Ethiopia (%) is shown from 1990 to 2019.
The chart tracks Ethiopia’s child mortality series over 1990–2019.
The health indicator is child mortality, measured as a percent.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Chart title, axis label, or annotation must name child mortality and percent, with x-axis spanning 1990–2019.
units.temporal_anchor: the opening Ethiopia/progress clause plus the child mortality clause
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly name child mortality as the health metric, or can it rely on the chart title?

units.meaning: Child mortality starts at 20.0% in 1990 and ends at 7.0% in 2019.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both endpoint values must be visible as labels, markers, or annotation on the line at 1990 and 2019.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'drop in child mortality from 20 % to 7 % since 1990'
units.reviewer_question: Should both 1990=20% and 2019=7% endpoints be explicitly labeled?

units.meaning: Child mortality falls by 13.0 percentage points from 1990 to 2019.
accepted_routes: 20% to 7%, a decline of 13 percentage points
units.visual_evidence_rule: A difference annotation or visible endpoint labels must make the 13-percentage-point change derivable.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'drop in child mortality from 20 % to 7 %'
units.reviewer_question: Is the 13-percentage-point drop required, or is the 20%→7% endpoint contrast sufficient?

units.meaning: Child mortality declines monotonically across every listed year from 1990 to 2019.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The plotted line must descend continuously across the full 1990–2019 x-axis without any upward segments.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video assert uninterrupted annual decline, or is a general downward trend enough?

units.meaning: By 2019, child mortality is about 65% lower than its 1990 level, or 35% of the 1990 level.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A percent-change annotation or a visible 1990 baseline of 20% must make the 65% decline or 35% retained level derivable.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'drop in child mortality' clause, if the video quantifies relative magnitude
units.reviewer_question: Should the relative 65% decline be included, or is it optional given the narration only states percentage-point endpoints?

optional_valid: Average annual reduction of about 0.45 percentage points per year: (20.0-7.0)/(2019-1990)=0.4483.
2019 is the lowest value in the series (7.0%).
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that improving health services caused the child mortality drop; the table only contains child mortality values.
Infrastructure improvements, population rank, or development rankings not present in the table.
Extrapolating beyond 2019 or predicting future child mortality.
Calling the 20%→7% change a 13% drop; it is 13 percentage points or a 65% relative decline.
Global or regional comparisons not present in the table.
notes: Only child mortality is in the table; infrastructure, population rank, and causal explanations are not supported. The key trade-off is whether to require the derived 13 pp and 65% reductions or only the endpoint/trend framing.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
